label: Gauss–Markov, BLUE and estimability — mastery test

items.stem: BLUE stands for:
items.explanation: BLUE means best linear unbiased estimator; the word best refers to the minimum-variance comparison among linear unbiased estimators.

items.stem: Which assumption is NOT required by the Gauss–Markov theorem?
options: Full column rank for the standard inverse form
items.explanation: Normality is not part of the Gauss–Markov assumptions; it is used for exact finite-sample distributional results.

items.stem: The ordinary OLS estimator when X has full column rank is:
items.explanation: The normal equations are X′Xβ̂=X′y, and full column rank permits inversion of X′X.

items.stem: Under V(u|X)=σ²I, the variance of OLS is:
items.explanation: Applying the matrix variance rule to (X′X)⁻¹X′u gives σ²(X′X)⁻¹.

items.stem: For X=[[1],[2]], calculate X′X.
items.explanation: X′X=1²+2²=5. Check by summing the squared entries of the column.

items.stem: If X′X=diag(4,9), what is the (1,1) element of Var(β̂)/σ²?
items.explanation: The inverse is diag(1/4,1/9), so the first variance factor is 1/4.

items.stem: A′β is estimable if and only if a belongs to:
items.explanation: Estimability requires a to be a linear combination of rows of X, equivalently a∈C(X′).

items.stem: If X has full column rank k, then:
options: Every linear function of β is estimable
items.explanation: Full column rank makes row(X)=Rᵏ, so every coefficient vector a belongs to the row space.

items.stem: The zero conditional mean assumption is primarily used to establish:
items.explanation: E(u|X)=0 makes E(β̂|X)=β after substituting the linear model.

items.stem: In the BLUE comparison, OLS is compared with:
items.explanation: The theorem's comparison class is specifically linear unbiased estimators.

items.stem: Which statements are correct? A. Normality is unnecessary for Gauss–Markov. B. OLS is linear in y. C. BLUE compares linear unbiased estimators. D. Spherical covariance includes zero off-diagonal covariances.
items.explanation: All four are correct: normality is not needed, OLS is linear in y, and σ²I specifies equal variances and zero covariances.
statements: Spherical covariance includes zero off-diagonal covariances.

A.why: The theorem does not require normality.

B.why: OLS is a matrix linear transformation of y.

C.why: The comparison class is linear and unbiased.

items.stem: For X=[[1,1],[2,0],[1,−1]], calculate the (1,1) element of X′X.
items.explanation: The first column has squared entries 1, 4 and 1; their sum is 6.

items.stem: For the same X, calculate the (2,2) element of X′X.
items.explanation: The second column has squared entries 1, 0 and 1; their sum is 2.

items.stem: For X=[[1,1],[2,0],[1,−1]], which statements are true? A. X′X is diagonal. B. rank(X)=2. C. Both β₁ and β₂ are estimable. D. X′X has determinant zero.
items.explanation: A, B and C are true. The determinant is 6×2=12, not zero.
statements: Spherical covariance includes zero off-diagonal covariances.

A.why: The theorem does not require normality.

B.why: OLS is a matrix linear transformation of y.

C.why: The comparison class is linear and unbiased.

items.stem: For the June 2026 design, the coefficient of y₂ in β̂₁ is:
items.explanation: β̂₁=(y₁+2y₂+y₃)/6, so the coefficient of y₂ is 2/6=1/3.

items.stem: If two columns of X are identical, which function is generally estimable?
items.explanation: The fitted mean depends on the sum along the shared column direction, while the difference is not identified.

items.stem: For any competing linear unbiased estimator Cy with CX=I, write C=(X′X)⁻¹X′+D. The restriction on D is:
items.explanation: Subtracting the OLS unbiasedness identity from CX=I gives DX=0.

items.stem: Which statements about the BLUE variance comparison are true? A. Var(Cy)−Var(β̂)=σ²DD′. B. DD′ is positive semidefinite. C. The difference can be negative in some direction. D. OLS is minimum variance in the linear unbiased class.
items.explanation: A, B and D are true; a′DD′a=||D′a||²≥0, so the difference cannot be negative in any direction.
statements: Spherical covariance includes zero off-diagonal covariances.

B.why: OLS is a matrix linear transformation of y.

items.stem: For the June 2026 design, calculate det(X′X).
items.explanation: X′X=diag(6,2), so its determinant is 12. This confirms full column rank.

items.stem: For β̂₂=(y₁−y₃)/2 and independent errors each with variance σ², find Var(β̂₂)/σ².
items.explanation: The variance is (1/4)(σ²+σ²)=σ²/2; the coefficient squares must be summed.
